opening: We evaluate workbook formulas with excelize (current main branch) through the cell value calculation API, and a handful of logical and matrix formulas disagree with Excel.

requirements.m01: Checking whether a cell holds a number reports TRUE for a cell that holds the logical value TRUE, both for a single cell reference and for a one-cell range; a logical is not a number, so the answer must be FALSE. The logical OR formula is also off: a range or array argument must count as true as soon as any one of its elements is true (non-zero numbers, or the text TRUE), text that is neither TRUE nor FALSE must give the wrong-type error (the one Excel shows for an argument of the wrong kind), and empty arguments are skipped. OR's result must also be a logical value, as in Excel, not the text TRUE: OR(1)*1 must give 1 and ISTEXT(OR(1)) must be FALSE. Aggregates over ranges that mix numbers and logicals (average including logicals, maximum, minimum, standard deviation) must give Excel's results.
requirements.m02: The matrix determinant formula gives a wrong result for a single-cell (1 by 1) matrix: the determinant of a one-element matrix is that element itself (5 for {5}, -3 for {-3}). Matrix inversion, which relies on determinants, must give correct results for small matrices too.
requirements.m03: An IF formula given only a condition and a value-if-true (no third argument) returns the wrong thing when the condition is false: it must return FALSE, as Excel does, while a true condition still returns the value-if-true.

closing: Results should match what Excel shows for the same workbook; the rest of the formula engine must keep working as it does now.
